papers.title: Why is target trial emulation not being used in health technology assessment real-world data submissions?
papers.one_line: An ISPOR 2024 issue panel reports that despite HTA guidance in place since 2022, no NICE real-world data submission has explicitly used target trial emulation, and the panel names lack of expertise and absent reporting standards as the reasons.
papers.what_was_done: A conference issue-panel report combines a search of NICE appraisals, audience polling and three stakeholder perspectives (HTA agency, manufacturer, consultancy). A search of NICE appraisals identified no submission explicitly using target trial emulation, although the framework is central to the NICE real-world evidence framework published in 2022. Peer-reviewed publications mentioning the framework rose exponentially from 2020 in a search conducted on 17 May 2024 using the terms 'target trial', 'target trial emulation' and 'trial emulation'. Audience polling identified lack of expertise and experience as the main barrier, and attendees expressed distrust that HTA agencies would accept such evidence. A worked NICE case study of an external control arm for a single-arm trial in a rare non-small-cell lung cancer subgroup is described: the committee could not judge whether best-practice design principles were followed, whether residual bias was addressed, or how large the missing-data problem was, because the analysis was complete-case with a prespecified confounder list. The report supplies no effect estimates, no sample sizes and no quantitative comparison of emulated and randomized results.

future_research.gap: No reporting standard exists for emulation studies, so an emulation performed by a manufacturer need not be identifiable as one in a submission
future_research.quote: Additionally, R Reynolds noted that there are currently no standard reporting guidelines for TTE

future_research.gap: Expertise in the approach is the binding constraint on its use in health technology assessment
future_research.quote: the main barrier to conducting TTE studies was lack of expertise and experience with the approach

problems.evidence: A NICE committee assessing an external control arm could not determine whether design principles had been met or whether residual bias had been handled, and had no threshold against which to make that determination. The remedy offered was descriptive: complete a data-suitability tool and describe the emulation as a protocol. Nothing in the account converts committee concern into a pass or fail rule on residual confounding or sensitivity analysis.
problems.quote: The committee also commented that it was not possible to assess whether best-practice study design principles had been followed and whether confounding and residual bias had been robustly addressed.

problems.evidence: A manufacturer representative advocating the framework at the same panel had to state explicitly that it is not a failsafe, and that questions which cannot be framed as a pragmatic trial fall outside it. That the caution needs stating in a decision-making forum shows the label is read as a warrant rather than as a description of which assumptions remain.
problems.quote: While an advocate for the TTE approach, he cautioned that TTE is not a failsafe

problems.evidence: No reporting standard for emulation studies exists, so an emulation actually performed by a manufacturer may not be documented as one in a submission. Without a standard, the design decisions, phenotype logic and rejected protocol variants behind a submitted analysis are not recoverable by the appraisal committee that has to judge it.
problems.quote: Additionally, R Reynolds noted that there are currently no standard reporting guidelines for TTE

problems.evidence: The case for the framework in this setting rests on one replication: a prior observational study reported statins reducing small cell lung cancer risk by 77% and the emulation found no effect, matching meta-analyses of randomized trials. That single question is then used to argue the framework enables regulatory-grade inference in general, with no argument connecting the statin result to the effectiveness questions actually posed in appraisals.
problems.quote: however Dickerman found that the TTE per protocol and intention-to-treat analyses reported no effect of statins on lung cancer

problems.evidence: The appraisal committee questioned whether all relevant confounders were captured and how much data were missing, and could not resolve either question from the submission. Data fitness was contested narratively at committee, after the study existed; there was no prior threshold on confounder capture or missingness that would have stopped the analysis or ruled the data source out.
problems.quote: Further, results were based on complete case analysis and confounders were taken from a prespecified list which led the committed to question whether all relevant confounders were captured and the magnitude of missing data.

papers.title: [The emulation of clinical trials with real-world data: development and application of target trial].
papers.one_line: A Chinese-language methods review proposes grading emulation evidence by combining ROBINS-I with GRADE and reports the RCT-DUPLICATE tally of 24 of 32 emulations meeting regulatory agreement, 21 estimate agreement and 24 test agreement.
papers.what_was_done: A narrative review sets out design steps for emulation with real-world data: defining intervention and outcome, eligibility criteria, sample size estimation, absence of blinding, statistical analysis, and choice of time zero. It advises against placebo comparators and recommends a comparator known to have no effect on the endpoint or a known active comparator, and states that a confirmatory emulation should have a sample size exceeding that of the trial it emulates. Three agreement criteria taken from the replication literature are described: regulatory agreement (same direction and statistical significance), estimate agreement (the emulation point estimate inside the trial 95% confidence interval), and test agreement (no statistically significant standardized difference), with the Z statistic written out. Of the 32 published RCT-DUPLICATE emulations, 24 met regulatory agreement, 21 estimate agreement and 24 test agreement, using 1:1 nearest-neighbor propensity score matching with a 0.01 caliper on 120 preselected covariates. Sources of discrepancy are classified into emulation differences across population, intervention, comparator, outcome and time, and into residual confounding and chance. A table compares ROBINS-I and GRADE and states that GRADE evidence grading is incompletely considered and coarsely divided; the review concludes that a grading system for emulations built from the two tools requires further discussion and better appraisal tools. No new data are analyzed.

future_research.gap: No appraisal instrument yet grades the evidence produced by an emulation; the review only opens the question
future_research.quote: This review preliminarily discusses the standard of evidence quality evaluation in target trial emulation.

problems.evidence: The review reaches for ROBINS-I plus GRADE to grade emulations and records that ROBINS-I covers only bias and ignores design, sample size and power, while GRADE grades coarsely. It concludes that a combined instrument still needs to be built. Grading emulation evidence is therefore an open construction problem, not a settled threshold.
problems.quote: This review preliminarily discusses the standard of evidence quality evaluation in target trial emulation.

problems.evidence: Uneven data quality is stated as the motivating premise, and the response offered is a data governance plan and combining sources or verifying an effect across data types. No quantitative fitness criterion is proposed and no described condition would stop a planned emulation.
problems.quote: Real-world data (RWD) can provide a robust data basis for comparative research, but the quality is uneven.

problems.evidence: The framework is presented as the mechanism that raises the evidence grade of an observational study: specifying exposure, eligibility, time zero, sample size and analysis in advance is described as converting real-world data into real-world evidence. The assumption burden that remains after those steps, chiefly unmeasured confounding, is acknowledged only as needing further research.
problems.quote: This review introduces the target trial emulation, in which researchers, using RWD and following the design of clinical trials, define exposure and outcome in advance, set eligibility criteria, determine the time zero, estimate sample size, and plan statistical analysis, to enhance the quality of evidence for observational studies.

papers.title: Improving the quality of evidence production in rehabilitation. Results of the 5th Cochrane Rehabilitation Methodological Meeting.
papers.one_line: An editorial introducing the 5th Cochrane Rehabilitation Methodological Meeting places target trial emulation among the observational designs recommended for a field whose interventions are formally defined as complex and where most authors mislabel their own study design.
papers.what_was_done: An editorial reports a September 2023 methodological meeting in Milan and introduces two special sections. Seven international working groups covered meta-epidemiology of randomized trials in rehabilitation, observational designs including the IDEAL framework and target trial emulation, single-case experimental designs, complex intervention studies, health services research and qualitative studies, with two further papers on question formulation and a road map for evidence production. Three prior experiences motivated the agenda: a research definition of rehabilitation developed with 80 global stakeholders that positions rehabilitation as a complex intervention; work with the World Health Organization on the Package of Interventions for Rehabilitation, whose overviews of Cochrane reviews found randomized trial evidence scarce and often low quality; and rapid living reviews during the COVID-19 pandemic that found widespread mislabeling of study designs. No data, sample sizes or estimates are reported; the document sets the agenda for the papers that follow.

future_research.gap: Randomized trials cannot supply the range of evidence the field needs, which forces designs whose assumption burden the field is not equipped to judge
future_research.quote: RCTs currently do not and in all likelihood cannot answer the range of research questions arising from practice information needs to provide all the evidence we need to treat our patients.

problems.evidence: Emulation is placed on the menu of designs for rehabilitation at the same meeting that adopts a research definition treating rehabilitation as a complex intervention, referred to Medical Research Council guidance. Neither the treatment versions of a rehabilitation program nor the unit at which it would be assigned, patient, therapist or service, is specified anywhere in the agenda.
problems.quote: observational study designs – specifically the IDEAL Framework (Idea, Development, Exploration, Assessment, Long-term study) and its potential implementation in rehabilitation and the Target Trial Emulation framework

problems.evidence: The field's own research definition classifies its interventions as complex, meaning a bundle of components delivered with variation in intensity, duration and provider. A protocol that names one such bundle as a treatment strategy is silently pooling versions that the definition itself says differ, and no procedure for deciding which versions belong together is offered.
problems.quote: This definition positions rehabilition as a complex intervention

problems.evidence: Rapid reviews during the pandemic found most authors in the field naming their design incorrectly, and the editorial attributes this to research being conducted by clinicians without methodological support. In a field where the design label and the method used come apart routinely, an emulation label carries no information about which assumptions the analysis actually took on.
problems.quote: What we found is that a tremendous level of methodological confusion appeared toexist in rehabilitation research, with a mislabelling of study designs by most authors

papers.title: Causal inference using observational intensive care unit data: a scoping review and recommendations for future practice.
papers.one_line: A scoping review of 79 intensive care causal-inference studies found only 30 (38%) reported all five target trial components and only seven (9%) mentioned all three causal assumptions, with positivity unmentioned in 54 (68%).
papers.what_was_done: Eight databases were searched to March 2023; 2,184 unique records yielded 79 included studies published 2005 to 2023 that estimate effects of time-varying treatments in adult intensive care. Forty-eight (61%) used G methods, of which 42 used inverse probability of treatment weighting, five the parametric g-formula and one targeted minimum loss-based estimation; 31 (39%) used reinforcement learning. Reinforcement learning studies had a median of 9,782 patients (IQR 5,022 to 17,898) against 1,498 (IQR 606 to 3,407) for G-method studies, and relied on open-source databases 74% versus 23% of the time. Only eight of 48 G-method studies (17%) considered dynamic regimes despite dynamic regimes being the clinically relevant class. Eligibility criteria and outcome were reported in 78 (99%) of studies, but treatment strategies, follow-up and analysis plan were partly or not reported in 14 (18%), 16 (20%) and 33 (42%); all five components appeared in 30 (38%). Conditional exchangeability was unmentioned in 25 (32%), positivity in 54 (68%), and consistency was mentioned in nine (11%). Seventeen studies (22%) reported estimates both with and without adjustment for treatment-affected time-varying confounding, and in three the point estimate reversed direction, in two it moved away from the null and in eight toward it.

future_research.gap: Positivity is verifiable in principle but not in practice for time-varying treatments, and weight inspection detects violations without ruling them out
future_research.quote: The number of patient treatment histories that match the treatment regime of interest

future_research.gap: Reporting of causal assumptions is systematically worse in the reinforcement learning literature than in the G-methods literature
future_research.quote: All three assumptions were mentioned (or a check for potential violations was reported) in only seven (9%) studies

problems.evidence: A reinforcement learning analysis of 3,855 sepsis patients supported its optimal regime with an effective sample of a few dozen patient histories. The review states the effective sample shrinks with the number of treatment decisions, which is high in intensive care, and that adding patients does not raise it if the added patients were not treated according to the regime.
problems.quote: applied RL to a dataset of 3855 patients to find an optimal treatment regime for sepsis, but the effective sample size for this regime was only a few dozen

problems.evidence: Across 79 studies of time-varying intensive care treatments, positivity was unmentioned in 68% and checked in 25%, and the check offered is inspection of the estimated weight distribution, which the review itself says detects but cannot rule out violations. Eleven of the 20 studies that reported a check never named the assumption being checked. No study is reported as naming which treatment histories lacked support.
problems.quote: The positivity assumption remained unmentioned in 54 (68%), was mentioned in five (6%), and a check for potential violations was reported in 20 (25%) of the studies.

problems.evidence: Seven of 79 studies (9%) mentioned all three of conditional exchangeability, positivity and consistency. Exchangeability is not verifiable from data while positivity is, and the review has to make that distinction itself because the studies do not: an assumption that can be diagnosed and one that cannot are reported alike, or not at all.
problems.quote: All three assumptions were mentioned (or a check for potential violations was reported) in only seven (9%) studies

problems.evidence: Only 17 of 79 studies (22%) reported the estimate both with and without adjustment for treatment-affected time-varying confounding, and among those the point estimate reversed direction in three, moved away from the null in two and toward it in eight. The adjustment choice changed the answer wherever it was examined, and 78% of studies never examined it.
problems.quote: For most of these studies, the point estimates of the treatment effects varied substantially after adjusting for both baseline and TTC

problems.evidence: Intensive care treatment decisions are re-evaluated continually on the evolving patient state, yet 83% of G-method studies estimated static regimes and only seven of the eight dynamic-regime studies appeared from 2020 onward. The clinically relevant estimand is a dynamic regime under a monitoring process that is itself treatment-dependent, and the literature substitutes a static contrast for it.
problems.quote: Treatments of interest in the ICU are typically DTRs and, therefore, this type of treatments is expected to be the focus of CI research in the ICU.

problems.evidence: Many included studies compared receiving a treatment at some point during the stay against never receiving it, for instance systemic antifungal therapy in intensive care. Every timing, dose and duration is folded into one arm, and the review states the resulting effect is ill-defined. No procedure is offered for deciding which treatment versions may be pooled into one strategy.
problems.quote: As giving treatment ‘sometime during follow-up’ can be done in many ways, the estimated treatment effect is ill-defined and typically not truly of interest.

papers.title: Are Target Trial Emulations the Gold Standard for Observational Studies?: The Authors Respond.
papers.one_line: No independent text was retrieved: the cached full text for this record is byte-identical to L0439, the Pearce and Vandenbroucke commentary, so the authors' reply itself was not read.
papers.what_was_done: This record is the authors' reply in Epidemiology to correspondence about the commentary published under DOI 10.1097/EDE.0000000000001636. The text cached for it is the same 31,195-character preprint of the original commentary that was cached for L0439; the two files share an MD5 hash, and the tail of the file is the commentary's reference list ending at reference 40. The retrieval therefore resolved the reply's DOI to the parent article rather than to the reply. Recording findings here would duplicate the six findings already recorded against L0439 under a second identifier and would double-count one piece of evidence in the catalog. No quote, number or claim is attributed to this record. Re-extraction from the published reply is required before it can contribute; the reply is short correspondence and its content is not represented anywhere in this batch.

papers.title: Are Target Trial Emulations the Gold Standard for Observational Studies?
papers.one_line: A methodological critique argues that emulation cannot handle intractable confounding and that matching inside an emulation discards data without gaining validity, citing a vaccine comparison that dropped 43% of participants, from 764,803 to 439,684.
papers.what_was_done: A commentary distinguishes the general emulation approach from a matched variant in which exposed and unexposed are made alike on key variables, and argues both against the framework as a default and against matching within it. Worked examples are quantitative: a comparative effectiveness study of BNT162b2 versus mRNA-1273 in US veterans went from 764,803 participants to 439,684 in producing 219,842 matched pairs, a 43% reduction, leaving 2,016 infections, 559 symptomatic, 411 hospitalizations, 125 intensive care admissions and 81 deaths, and a death risk ratio of 1.11 with 95% CI 0.69 to 1.91. A hypothetical two-category age match is used to show that matching reproduces a stratified analysis on fewer people. A second argument is that matching removes the ability to compare unadjusted and adjusted estimates, the change-in-estimate signal that indicates residual confounding; an unadjusted risk ratio of 2.0 falling to 1.9 and one falling to 1.4 are contrasted. The critique cites an emulation that recovered the expected protective effect of statins on mortality but found antihypertensives increasing mortality, against many randomized trials. Alternatives named are the test-negative design, difference-in-differences, instrumental variables, regression discontinuity, Mendelian randomization and triangulation.

future_research.gap: Confounding remains intractable for some questions no matter how well an emulation is executed, and no procedure identifies which questions those are in advance
future_research.quote: Thus, there are important situations where even the best possible TTE study that relies on emulating conditional randomization cannot answer a causal question.
future_research.locator: General limitations of the TTE approach

problems.evidence: One emulation recovered the randomized-trial answer for statins and mortality and simultaneously produced the wrong sign for antihypertensives and mortality, in the same design and the same data. Success on one exposure inside a study therefore carries no information about the next exposure, which is exactly what an extrapolation theory would have to supply and does not.
problems.quote: but found that the use of anti-hypertensives increased mortality, in contrast with the established findings of many RCTs
problems.locator: General limitations of the TTE approach

problems.evidence: Matching on confounders forces unadjusted and adjusted estimates to coincide, removing the change-in-estimate diagnostic that a conventional analysis provides; the analyst is left assuming no residual confounding. Reversed strategies and negative control outcomes are named as possible substitutes but are not part of the workflow, and the more direct diagnostic is unavailable by construction.
problems.quote: One is then left with the need to simply assume that there is no residual confounding, with few means to assess this
problems.locator: Specific problems of the matched-TTE design

problems.evidence: A cohort of 764,803 vaccinated veterans became 439,684 analyzed people in 219,842 matched pairs, a 43% loss, with the outcome counts falling to 81 deaths and a death risk ratio of 1.11 (95% CI 0.69 to 1.91). Database size did not translate into analyzable events once the design restriction was applied, and the discarded participants are never characterized.
problems.quote: reduced the analysed participants from 764,803 to 439,684, a reduction of 43%
problems.locator: Specific problems of the matched-TTE design

problems.evidence: The claim is that a matched emulation and a conventional covariate-adjusted analysis on the whole data set give an almost identical point estimate while the matched version is less precise. No published emulation is required to show that its design and estimator choice changed the answer, so the two analyses coexist with no evidence about which mattered.
problems.quote: the same aim can be achieved by not matching, using the whole data set and simply controlling for the same factors in the data analysis, usually with a gain in precision
problems.locator: Specific problems of the matched-TTE design

problems.evidence: The stated concern is that the formalism signals a level of rigor that the data cannot deliver when confounding is intractable, and that a design which looks like a randomized trial is easier to market to policy makers. The label is doing evidential work that the assumption burden does not support.
problems.quote: but the formalism of the TTE approach may suggest a level of methodological rigour that simply cannot be obtained in such situations
problems.locator: General limitations of the TTE approach

problems.evidence: Design flaws that emulation repairs, such as misaligned time zero, and the undiagnosable assumption of conditional exchangeability are treated as one package under the framework label. The critique separates them and shows that for vaccinated versus unvaccinated comparisons the second is beyond repair, while nothing in reporting practice marks that distinction.
problems.quote: Thus, there are important situations where even the best possible TTE study that relies on emulating conditional randomization cannot answer a causal question.
problems.locator: General limitations of the TTE approach

papers.title: Comparison of the Test-negative Design and Cohort Design With Explicit Target Trial Emulation for Evaluating COVID-19 Vaccine Effectiveness.
papers.one_line: In 546,810 matched veteran pairs, a cohort emulation and a test-negative design gave similar BNT162b2 effectiveness in rich data, but with a limited variable set the cohort estimate fell to 72.0% while the test-negative estimate rose to 83.4%.
papers.what_was_done: Nationwide US Department of Veterans Affairs data were used to build four designs on the same population: an explicit target trial emulation, a case-control sample of that cohort, a sample restricted to person-days with a test, and a test-negative design. Of 571,307 eligible vaccinated individuals, 546,810 were matched to unvaccinated comparators; over 22 weeks there were 2,808 documented infections, 1,308 symptomatic. The 22-week risk ratios were 0.30 (95% CI 0.28 to 0.35) for documented infection and 0.26 (0.22 to 0.30) for symptomatic Covid-19. From day 28, emulated effectiveness for symptomatic Covid-19 was 87.2% (85.4% to 91.8%) against randomized-trial rate-ratio benchmarks of 95.0% (90.3% to 97.6%) and 91.3% (89.0% to 93.2%). Restricting to person-days with a test gave 80.4% (76.6% to 83.2%) and 87.0% (84.3% to 92.6%). Negative control outcome risks were nearly identical between groups and testing frequencies were similar. Repeating both designs on a limited variable set inverted the picture: the cohort estimate fell to 72.0% (68.9% to 74.4%) for documented infection while the test-negative estimate rose to 83.4% (82.2% to 84.5%), and a further stripped test-negative analysis reached 87.0% (86.4% to 87.5%).

future_research.gap: Agreement between the two designs is a property of this data source and period, not a transferable result
future_research.quote: However, the observed consistency in estimates across designs may not hold for a different population, data source, or time-period

future_research.gap: The direction of design-induced bias cannot be predicted in a new application
future_research.quote: However, the direction of bias in other applications is difficult to predict and may differ for the cohort design and test-negative design.

problems.evidence: The same two designs on the same veterans, run once with the full variable set and once with a limited one, moved in opposite directions: the cohort emulation to 72.0% and the test-negative design to 83.4% for documented infection from day 28, against 87.2% for symptomatic disease in the full data. Data richness, not design, determined the answer, and no stated fitness criterion would have blocked the limited-data analysis.
problems.quote: In our analyses in limited datasets, the estimated vaccine effectiveness was biased downward in the cohort design and biased upward in the test-negative design

problems.evidence: The test-negative design assesses eligibility, exposure and covariates at the time of testing rather than at time zero, which is a healthcare-use event occurring after baseline. Conditioning on it is equivalent to adjusting for post-baseline variables and can open a collider path. Here the induced bias was small because testing frequencies were similar between arms, which is an empirical accident of this system rather than a property of the design.
problems.quote: This is equivalent to adjusting for post-baseline variables in the target trial and thus may induce selection bias.

problems.evidence: The day-28 landmark was chosen so that estimates could be set beside prior randomized trials, and the two designs implement it differently: the emulation excludes early events in both arms while the test-negative design excludes them only among the vaccinated. The choice of grid is driven by the comparison the analyst wants to make, and the test-negative estimates correspond to no defined follow-up window at all.
problems.quote: In the test-negative design, the effectiveness estimates do not correspond to a well-defined follow-up period and thus are not directly comparable with those from the randomized

problems.evidence: Rather than declare the emulation a success or failure against the trial, the comparison is reported as 87.2% (85.4% to 91.8%) against 95.0% (90.3% to 97.6%), with the residual gap attributed to an older and sicker population and to undocumented baseline infection, and with a separate note that risk ratios and rate ratios are not the same estimand. What is not supplied is any calibrated measure of that gap: the estimand difference is discussed in words and never quantified or partitioned.
problems.quote: similar to, but slightly lower than, estimates from the randomized trial, which may be partially explained by the inclusion of a more vulnerable population

problems.evidence: Negative control outcomes and a randomized benchmark are run inside the emulation rather than appended to it: risks for the negative control outcome were nearly identical across arms, and the first ten days of follow-up showed the same infection pattern in both groups. The workflow does not generalize as stated, because the benchmark existed only because a trial of this vaccine had already been run, and the negative control was interpreted qualitatively with no threshold for how much divergence would have invalidated the analysis.
problems.quote: explicitly emulated a target trial using follow-up data and evaluated the potential for confounding using negative controls and benchmarking to a randomized

problems.evidence: The shortfall of the emulated estimate against the randomized benchmark is attributed to a more vulnerable population with respect to age and comorbidity burden, plus undocumented infection depleting susceptibles among the unvaccinated. Neither the sampling difference from the trial population nor the residual confounding is quantified, so the two explanations for the same gap are never separated.
problems.quote: similar to, but slightly lower than, estimates from the randomized trial, which may be partially explained by the inclusion of a more vulnerable population

papers.title: Reporting of Observational Studies Explicitly Aiming to Emulate Randomized Trials: A Systematic Review.
papers.one_line: Across 200 studies that explicitly claimed to emulate a target trial, only 58% completely reported how the emulation was done, 37% named a potential unmeasured confounder, 13% reported relying on more than one causal assumption and 10% were prospectively registered.
papers.what_was_done: Four databases were searched from March 2012 to October 2022 with forward citation tracking of five seminal papers; 3,133 unique records yielded 200 included studies, 168 (84%) published from January 2020 onward, spanning 26 fields, most often infectious disease (43, 22%), cardiology (30, 15%) and oncology (30, 15%). One hundred thirty-one (66%) used electronic health records, claims or linked data. Individual protocol items were mostly reported: eligibility criteria 193 (97%), treatment strategies 191 (96%), assignment 173 (87%), outcome 196 (98%), follow-up 186 (93%), analysis plan 194 (97%), but causal contrast only 146 (73%); 115 studies (58%) reported all of them and 87 (44%) gave both the target trial protocol and its emulation. Twenty studies (10%) reported prospective registration. Variables adjusted for were reported by 187 (94%) but how they were selected by 77 (39%). Sensitivity analyses for statistical or causal assumptions appeared in 131 (66%), most often as an alternative confounding adjustment (42 of 131, 32%). Exchangeability was stated by 158 (79%) and 26 studies (13%) reported reliance on more than one causal assumption. Forty-three (22%) cited a reporting guideline, usually STROBE, with no qualitative difference in reporting when they did.

future_research.gap: No consensus reporting guideline exists for emulations, and general observational guidelines omit the causal contrast and time-zero items
future_research.quote: Using the target trial framework is neither necessary nor sufficient for obtaining valid causal effect estimates from observational analyses

problems.evidence: Of 200 explicit emulations, 73 (37%) named a potential unmeasured confounder and 26 (13%) reported relying on more than one causal assumption, while 158 (79%) asserted exchangeability. Studies state the assumption they cannot check and stay silent on the rest, so a reader cannot tell from a report which assumptions were diagnosed and which were merely asserted.
problems.quote: We found that only 73 studies (37%) reported potential unmeasured confounders.

problems.evidence: Twenty-six of 200 studies (13%) reported reliance on more than one causal assumption at all, and where sensitivity analyses were run the most common form (42 of 131, 32%) was swapping one confounding adjustment method for another. Nothing in this corpus varies several violated assumptions jointly; the modal sensitivity analysis varies the estimator, not an assumption.
problems.quote: reported reliance on more than 1 causal assumption
problems.locator: Reporting of Further Items That Relate to the Target Trial Emulation

problems.evidence: Twenty of 200 studies (10%) reported prospective registration and 16 of those 20 said where the registration could be found. Ninety percent of published emulations therefore offer no evidence that the target trial protocol they analyze was fixed before the data were examined, while the inference proceeds as if it had been.
problems.quote: reported the study was prospectively registered
problems.locator: Reporting of Further Items That Relate to the Target Trial Emulation

problems.evidence: The causal contrast was the least reported protocol item at 146 of 200 (73%), against 93% for follow-up and 97% for the analysis plan. More than a quarter of explicit emulations report an analysis and an effect measure without stating which contrast the number estimates, so the estimand has to be inferred from the estimator.
problems.quote: the follow-up period (186 [93%]), a causal contrast (146 [73%], and an analysis plan (194 [97%])
problems.locator: Characteristics of Target Trials and How They Were Emulated

problems.evidence: The review states plainly that using the framework is neither necessary nor sufficient for a valid causal estimate, and its own numbers show why the label cannot stand in for an assumption audit: 58% completely reported the emulation and 37% named an unmeasured confounder. A prior review using ROBINS-I found only 3% of 77 non-explicit observational studies specified all protocol items, so the label marks an improvement in reporting, not a resolution of assumptions.
problems.quote: Using the target trial framework is neither necessary nor sufficient for obtaining valid causal effect estimates from observational analyses

problems.evidence: The extraction protocol had to rule that truncating weights to satisfy positivity does not count as reporting the positivity assumption, which means the practice was common enough in this corpus to need a rule. Weight handling is offered where a statement about which histories lack support belongs.
problems.quote: We did not regard practices that may assess a causal assumption (eg, truncation of weights to satisfy the assumption of positivity) as reporting the assumption.

problems.evidence: Emulations are routinely compared with randomized trials, and the review notes the differences can arise from many sources and that better protocol reporting might help understand them. Understanding is offered as the remedy for a discrepancy that is never decomposed, and in a corpus where 27% do not state the causal contrast, the two estimands being compared are often not both known.
problems.quote: Differences in effect estimates between target trial emulations and randomized clinical trials may arise due to various factors.

papers.title: Current practices in studies applying the target trial emulation framework: a protocol for a systematic review.
papers.one_line: A systematic review protocol registers the observation that no existing reporting checklist expects a statement of whether the data were judged fit for purpose, and that whether emulations should be pre-registered is unsettled.
papers.what_was_done: A protocol for a systematic review of emulation practice specifies searches of Medline, Embase (including medRxiv entries), PsycINFO, Scopus, Web of Science, the Cochrane Library, the ISRCTN registry and ClinicalTrials.gov with no time restriction, duplicate screening, duplicate extraction and third-reviewer adjudication, and narrative synthesis reported to PRISMA. Extraction covers study design, data source, analysis, results, interpretation and dissemination. The protocol states that risk of bias assessment will not be included and that excluding non-English databases may introduce language bias. Its motivating argument is that emulations sit between two reporting traditions, CONSORT because they mimic randomized trials and STROBE because they are observational, that neither expects a statement about whether the data were judged fit for purpose for the emulation, and that pre-registration is expected for randomized trials but not for observational studies. No results, no sample sizes and no effect estimates are reported; the document is a plan.

future_research.gap: Whether emulations should be pre-registered is undecided
future_research.quote: At present, there is uncertainty over whether pre-registration should be mandatory, or at least encouraged, for target trial emulation studies.

future_research.gap: Existing checklists may not capture the features specific to emulation
future_research.quote: It may also be that existing checklists are not sufficient to capture all the nuances that exist in target trial emulation.

problems.evidence: Neither CONSORT nor STROBE asks how the data were evaluated and judged fit for purpose for the emulation, so the fitness assessment appears in a report only when an author volunteers it. The protocol draws the consequence itself: reports on data quality that do appear may be selective. There is no instrument, and therefore no threshold at which a data source would be ruled out.
problems.quote: For example, explicit statements on quality assessment such as how the data have been evaluated and judged to be fit-for-purpose for trial emulation are not expected by existing guidelines.

problems.evidence: Pre-registration is expected of randomized trials and not of observational studies, and the protocol records that whether it should be required of emulations remains an open question in 2023. An emulation is analyzed as though its target trial were fixed in advance while nothing in practice obliges the analyst to have fixed it before seeing the data.
problems.quote: At present, there is uncertainty over whether pre-registration should be mandatory, or at least encouraged, for target trial emulation studies.

problems.evidence: Regulatory use is expected to require a relevance assessment demonstrating that the real-world data are fit for purpose, yet the protocol has just established that no reporting guideline asks for one. The regulatory expectation exists without a corresponding item that any study is required to report or any level it must reach.
problems.quote: Clear reporting of these steps is critical especially for regulatory purposes that may require relevance assessments demonstrating fit-for-purpose of the RWD.

problems.evidence: Two general checklists are available and the protocol judges that neither is sufficient for the features specific to emulation, so no reporting artifact distinguishes which assumptions an emulation could diagnose from those it could not. The planned review will not assess risk of bias, so it will describe reporting completeness without connecting it to assumption burden.
problems.quote: It may also be that existing checklists are not sufficient to capture all the nuances that exist in target trial emulation.

papers.title: Target Trial Emulation to Improve Causal Inference from Observational Data: What, Why, and How?
papers.one_line: A methods review argues emulation should become the standard for observational studies of interventions, citing a review in which 57% of observational studies had immortal time bias and 44% depletion of susceptibles, while stating the framework is not a magic bullet against residual confounding.
papers.what_was_done: A tutorial review sets out the components of a target trial protocol and their emulation, using a comparison of renin-angiotensin system inhibitors against calcium channel blockers in advanced chronic kidney disease as the worked example. The argument for the framework rests on design errors rather than confounding: a cited review found 57% of observational studies affected by immortal time bias and 44% by depletion of susceptibles or prevalent user selection bias, and the discrepancy between the randomized IDEAL trial of dialysis timing and the observational literature that found a survival advantage for late start is attributed to starting follow-up before or after treatment assignment. Three designs are mapped to question types: active comparator new user, sequential trials, and clone censor weight for grace periods, treatment duration or biomarker-triggered initiation. Each protocol component is worked through with its failure modes, including eligibility criteria that cannot be emulated because claims data record that a test was done but not its result, surveillance bias when one arm is measured more often, and the fact that only per-protocol effects are available in observational data. Benchmarking against trials and negative control outcomes are recommended as confidence-building devices. No new estimates are produced.

future_research.gap: Benchmarking and negative control outcomes need prior trial evidence, so the questions with least evidence are the ones where the checks are unavailable
future_research.quote: Both benchmarking and negative outcome controls require strong subject matter knowledge, often derived from previous randomized trial evidence.
future_research.locator: Increasing Confidence in Causality from Observational Studies

problems.evidence: A tutorial arguing for the framework as the new standard has to state twice that the label does not settle anything: that studies claiming to use it are not all applying it correctly, and that it is not a magic bullet against unmeasured or residual confounding. The claim being made in the field is stronger than what the framework delivers, which is repair of design errors such as immortal time bias.
problems.quote: Furthermore, not every observational study claiming to use “target trial emulation” is applying the framework correctly.

problems.evidence: Claims databases record that a test was performed and not its result, so an eligibility criterion such as serum potassium below 5.0 mmol/L cannot be emulated. The prescribed response is a compromise between the trial one wants and the trial the data permit, which silently redefines the population and therefore the estimand. Nothing in the account requires the resulting data-defined population to be described or the difference to be quantified.
problems.quote: Often, a compromise is necessary between the ideal target trial one would like to emulate and the target trial one can emulate with the available data sources.

problems.evidence: Only per-protocol effects are estimable without randomization, yet the review records that investigators routinely label the effect of initiating treatment an intention-to-treat effect, which is not the quantity of the same name in a trial. The reported estimand and the estimated one come apart by convention, and the reader of a published hazard ratio has no way to tell which is meant.
problems.quote: However, investigators often refer to the effect of initiating treatment as the intention-to-treat effect in observational studies, which is thus different from the equivalently named effect in randomized trials.

problems.evidence: The sicker arm gets more eGFR measurements and therefore more detected outcomes, and a diagnostic is supplied: compare the number of measurements per arm during follow-up. The entry stays open because the diagnostic detects the imbalance without correcting it, and the one obvious fix is forbidden, since restricting to patients with a given number of measurements would condition on post-baseline information and induce selection bias. The measurement process is acknowledged as outcome-relevant and still handled outside the causal model.
problems.quote: One can check for this problem by comparing the number of eGFR measurements between both arms during follow-up.

problems.evidence: Benchmarking and negative control outcomes are the two recommended devices for residual bias, and both are said to require subject matter knowledge usually derived from prior randomized trials; the review concludes that studies conducted before any trial evidence exists are therefore harder. The checks are available precisely where they are least needed, and neither is given a threshold or a place in a fixed workflow.
problems.quote: Both benchmarking and negative outcome controls require strong subject matter knowledge, often derived from previous randomized trial evidence.
problems.locator: Increasing Confidence in Causality from Observational Studies

problems.evidence: Diet, exercise, bariatric surgery and semaglutide can lower body mass index by the same amount with different effects on the outcome, so an effect attributed to the biomarker is an amalgamation over the interventions that produced it. The review's remedy is to reformulate the question around one intervention, which relocates the problem rather than solving it: no procedure is given for deciding which interventions may be pooled into one strategy when that reformulation is not available.
problems.quote: Therefore, the association between BMI and outcomes becomes an amalgamation of each of these interventions, which makes the association difficult to interpret.
problems.locator: Target trial Emulation Helps to Ask Causal Questions Relevant in Decision-Making

papers.title: Target Trial Emulation and Bias Through Missing Eligibility Data: An Application to a Study of Palivizumab for the Prevention of Hospitalization Due to Infant Respiratory Illness.
papers.one_line: Gestational age was missing for 2,814 of 8,294 (34%) high-risk infants, so restricting to complete eligibility data left a trial of 1,560 while imputation implied up to 2,500 more eligible infants, and only imputation before selection removed the resulting selection and collider bias.
papers.what_was_done: Simulation plus an application quantify the bias from restricting an emulation to individuals whose eligibility variables are observed. Simulations at n = 1,000,000 vary a missingness parameter driving observation through covariates, a parameter driving it through the eligibility variable itself, and the eligible fraction; three strategies are compared, complete-case restriction, restriction with adjustment for the induced collider, and multiple imputation of eligibility variables before selection. Bias in strategies 1 and 2 tracked the shift in the distribution of the eligibility variable and grew with both missingness parameters and with the size of the effect modification; collider adjustment changed little; the imputation strategy was unbiased within Monte Carlo error in all cases but its confidence intervals overcovered. The application used the Hospital Treatment Insights database linking dispensing records from 43 English hospitals to Hospital Episode Statistics for infants born 2010 to 2016, a source population of 8,294 high-risk infants with congenital heart disease or chronic lung disease. Gestational age was missing for 2,814 (34%), leaving 1,560 infants with complete eligibility data. Complete-case average causal effects were -0.003 and -0.01; imputation under missing at random gave -0.001 and -0.002; under missing not at random the range widened to -1.0% to 1.3% and -3.1% to 2.3%. No estimate was significant at 95%.

future_research.gap: The impact of missing eligibility data on an emulation is acknowledged as a limitation and almost never studied
future_research.quote: Although identified as a potential limitation, there is little work investigating the extent to which missing eligible data can impact the analysis of a target trial.

future_research.gap: The quantities that determine the size of the selection bias are not computable from the source population
future_research.quote: None of these characteristics can be calculated from the source population but could be inferred using external linked data sets.

problems.evidence: Missing gestational age for 2,814 of 8,294 infants (34%) made eligibility unidentifiable for a third of the source population, and the standard responses, excluding them or redefining the trial, are shown by simulation to be biased whenever an eligibility variable modifies the effect. The supplied procedure is to impute the eligibility variables before selection, which was unbiased in every simulated scenario. It does not close the entry: the missing-not-at-random version required the correct sensitivity parameters to be supplied, an assumed missing-at-random imputation under a truly missing-not-at-random mechanism showed notable bias, and inverse probability weighting for the same missingness failed outright.
problems.quote: Gestational age, however, is missing for 2,814 (34%) infants in the source population.

problems.evidence: Restricting to observed eligibility conditions on a variable caused by the covariates, opening a collider path and shifting the covariate distribution of the analyzed trial away from the eligible population. Imputation before selection is shown to remove both the selection and the collider component in simulation. The entry stays open because the collider here is created by the recording process rather than by an eligibility criterion built from healthcare use, and the direct collider adjustment, strategy 2, made almost no difference.
problems.quote: We demonstrated via simulation that an imputed TT can eliminate sources of selection and collider bias, improve the sample size of a TT, and allow users to investigate sensitivity to changes in the assumptions of the missing eligible data on effect size.

problems.evidence: A linked national source of 8,294 high-risk infants produced a trial of 1,560 once eligibility required complete gestational age, birth weight, deprivation score and ethnicity. Imputation implied more than 1,000 additional eligible infants under missing at random and nearly 2,500 more under missing not at random, so between 40% and 60% of the eligible population was invisible to the complete-case analysis.
problems.quote: The imputation model implies a high number of missing eligible participants, with over 1,000 more individuals under the MAR imputed trial, and up to nearly 2,500 more under MNAR.

problems.evidence: The correct variance procedure for the imputed emulation, bootstrap within multiple imputation, is described as computationally intensive enough to run for several hours even on a cluster, so the application fell back to a percentile bootstrap with single imputation, which overcovers. The alternative offered, a corrected pooled variance, is said to require complex methods. No default is available that is both correct and affordable.
problems.quote: A limitation of this method is the tendency of CIs to overcover.

problems.evidence: The three quantities that govern the size of the selection bias, the strength of the missingness mechanism, the number of missing eligible individuals and the size of the effect modification, cannot be computed from the source population. External linked data are named as the way to infer them, and are not part of the analysis performed. The validation source that would resolve the diagnostic sits outside the workflow.
problems.quote: None of these characteristics can be calculated from the source population but could be inferred using external linked data sets.

problems.evidence: The missing-not-at-random analysis varies two sensitivity parameters for the exposed and unexposed arms, setting each to 0 or -4, which shifted mean gestational age by 2.2 and 2.7 weeks and moved the effect between -3.1% and 2.3%. The paper labels this exploratory, and the exercise varies only the missingness assumption while confounding by indication, unmeasured adherence and diagnosis misclassification are all acknowledged and held fixed.
problems.quote: This highlights that, in practice, MNAR imputation is an exploratory technique

papers.title: Design considerations for observational studies of drugs for advanced cancer.
papers.one_line: A commentary on advanced-cancer real-world studies lets patients contribute to first, second, third and fourth line-of-treatment cohorts simultaneously for efficiency, and defines a comparator arm as docetaxel, cabazitaxel, enzalutamide, abiraterone or others.
papers.what_was_done: Three design challenges specific to advanced cancer are set out: a study drug can appear in several lines of treatment, several lines can be received before the outcome occurs, and treatment strategy is not defined at baseline in a real-world database. Two applied studies illustrate the proposed handling. A post-authorization safety study of Radium-223 versus other standard of care for fracture incidence in Swedish men with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer built separate cohorts for first, second, third and fourth lines of treatment, aligned time zero, eligibility and exposure assignment in each, allowed patients eligible for more than one line to enter all line-specific cohorts for efficiency, and pooled the cohorts on the assumption that the effect was homogeneous across lines. A study of adding erlotinib to gemcitabine in advanced pancreatic cancer set time zero at gemcitabine initiation, allowed erlotinib initiation within a 12-week grace period, cloned each eligible patient into both strategies, artificially censored person-time incompatible with the assigned strategy and used inverse probability weighting for baseline and post-baseline confounding. The causal contrast in both is the observational analogue of the per-protocol effect. No effect estimates, sample sizes or variance calculations are reported.

future_research.gap: Identification is conditional on a conjunction of unverifiable conditions that are stated together and never separated
future_research.quote: absence of unmeasured confounding, measurement error, and model misspecification (including models used to handle missing data), this approach will help identify the causal effect of well-specified treatment strategies.

problems.evidence: Patients eligible for more than one line of treatment were entered into every line-specific cohort, and the stated reason is efficiency. The four cohorts were then pooled on an assumed homogeneous effect across lines. The same person contributes correlated person-time to several cohorts at different calendar dates, and neither the correlation nor the calendar-time structure is addressed anywhere in the account.
problems.quote: For efficiency, we let patients contribute to all LoT-specific cohorts
problems.locator: Emulating a target trial to handle challenges with RWD

problems.evidence: The comparator strategy in the Radium-223 study is initiation of docetaxel, cabazitaxel, enzalutamide, abiraterone or unnamed others, four pharmacologically distinct agents plus an open category treated as one arm. No criterion is given for why these belong in one equivalence class, and the fracture outcome could plausibly differ across them.
problems.quote: Group 2: Initiate other standard of care (docetaxel, cabazitaxel, enzalutamide, abiraterone, others).

problems.evidence: The grace period for adding erlotinib is set at 12 weeks, justified only by the observation that erlotinib may be started a few weeks later than gemcitabine in routine care. No outcome-blind rule fixes the width, and in a disease described as highly lethal the grace-period width determines how much early mortality is assigned to each cloned strategy.
problems.quote: Initiate erlotinib (any dose) within the grace period: up to 12 weeks after gemcitabine initiation.

problems.evidence: The design stacks cloning, artificial censoring and inverse probability weighting on top of a cohort structure where a patient may appear in four line-of-treatment cohorts. Each device duplicates or reweights person-time, and the commentary specifies the point estimation in detail while saying nothing about how a confidence interval is obtained under those duplications.
problems.quote: Clones were used to classify patients into treatment strategies according to their baseline data

problems.evidence: The causal contrast is named as the observational analogue of the per-protocol effect rather than left implicit behind a hazard ratio, and the machinery producing it is spelled out: artificial censoring to keep compliant person-time and weighting to recover the effect under complete adherence. What remains unaddressed is that the estimand is defined over patients whose baseline data were compatible with a 12-week grace period, a subpopulation that is never described, and no effect measure or its scale is reported.
problems.quote: Specification of treatment strategies that consider post-baseline events. Use of artificial censoring to select the person-time compliant with the treatment strategies and inverse probability of treatment weighting to estimate the effect under complete adherence

problems.evidence: The concluding claim conditions identification on the joint absence of unmeasured confounding, measurement error and model misspecification including the missing-data models. Three assumptions that will in practice be violated together are named in one clause, and no sensitivity analysis of any kind, single or joint, is proposed.
problems.quote: absence of unmeasured confounding, measurement error, and model misspecification (including models used to handle missing data), this approach will help identify the causal effect of well-specified treatment strategies.
